chapter_note: The chapter opens with a formulaic dialogue frame (late). The oldest layer appears in ¶2–3: impersonal cosmological exposition about the Mother of Life and the First Man grieving for their afflicted children in the Darkness, including the five sons motif. The second half (¶4–5) shows clear pastoral/institutional drift (holy church, persecution, repentance/gehenna), consistent with the high editorial fatigue score; these read as later editorial/community application rather than the old teaching core.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic opening attribution (“Once again the enlightener speaks to his disciples”) is hagiographic/compilational framing; not part of the old teaching layer.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.147⟩ The first who grieves is the first Mother of Life. She is sad because of her children who are set in affliction, for they were conjoined with the Darkness and the [poi]son. They have been bound with the entire ruling-power. For what was she grieving, [wa]tching over them taking these afflictions? Whenever she might [s]ee them and how suffering is brought upon them, she shall grieve and be unhappy on account of them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal cosmological explanation (Mother of Life; children bound in Darkness; ‘ruling-power’ as cosmic constraint) with no ecclesial or citation apparatus; reads as direct systematic mythic mechanics → core teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.148⟩ [The s]econd one who is troubled of heart is the First Man, whose [great]ness and kingdom is established in the li[ght] ship [...]. And he too is troubled of heart because of his five sons who are set in the midst of danger. For any time he may see that they are given trouble, always he might hear the sound of their weeping as they cry out because of the blows and wounds of the enemy who assaults them daily; and as he sees them like this constantly, he shall g[ri]eve and mourn on account of his [s]o[n]s.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core cosmological beings (First Man; light ship; five sons) in explanatory, process-oriented voice (“whenever… he may see/hear… he shall grieve”), describing ongoing light-dark assault mechanics rather than institutional exhortation.

First-person self-identification (“The third one who grieves am I”) tied to ‘holy church’, persecution, ‘Light Mind’ placed in the church—an institutional/hagiographic application consistent with second-half pastoral drift. Even if it echoes mythic language, it is not the old impersonal cosmological layer.

Soteriological exhortation and disciplinary vocabulary (refused hope, certainty of truth, repentance, reconciliation, mercy) plus eschatological threat (“gehenna for ever”) indicates later pastoral/paraenetic layer rather than core cosmological exposition.
